title: Computer Architecture
description: Can trace machine-level execution from digital logic and assembly through the memory hierarchy — and can locate where a value lives when a result is wrong.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can assemble a small program, record the registers it uses, and trace one instruction through fetch-decode-execute — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement a selected hardware project that passes provided tests, document an assembly program's register and memory use, and distinguish registers, RAM and persistent storage in a short note.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently trace a full instruction cycle on a machine they built or simulated, locate a given value in the memory hierarchy, and show which path an address takes.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a wrong result as a logic, datapath or memory-hierarchy mistake, cite the failing instruction and the storage level involved, and defend why a cache miss is not a software bug.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's CPU or assembly work, name a step they skipped in the instruction cycle, and teach how a load walks the memory hierarchy on an unfamiliar ISA or simulator.
